findings: The new capture expands Klarna-specific prohibited business categories beyond old charities, political organizations and B2B to money services/crypto, stored-value/gift cards, insolvency/debt/fines/bail services, gambling/lotteries, direct marketing and fundraising/crowdfunding. The new text spells the retained B2B category as 'Business-to-business (BTB)', apparently a label discrepancy; do not infer a changed B2B policy from that spelling alone. Stripe-wide restrictions are additional, and Dashboard payment-method settings are an account eligibility route, not proof of approval (old raw lines 10-18; new raw lines 11-26; source line 17).

A new dated statement says EU consumer marketing of Klarna credit products faces additional CCD2 disclosures beginning 2026-11-20, requiring Klarna pre-approved copy and applicable country disclosures. It names country-specific guideline links for AT, BE, DK, FI, FR, DE, GR, HU, IT, SK and SE. This is a captured Stripe/Klarna statement, not independent verification of live law or permission; it applies to marketing credit products to consumers in the EU, not every merchant or payment (new raw lines 28-34; old raw lines 20-24; source lines 13, 19).

Unchanged UK marketing text requires Klarna-approved advertising and warns of criminal-charge risk; PMME is recommended for Klarna brand compliance. Do not generalize the Element's brand handling to satisfying every UK/EU legal disclosure or to proving shopper finance eligibility. Klarna separately decides whether a customer may use it, while Stripe acquires and settles merchant funds; marketing display does not create a payment (old raw lines 20-24, 30-39; new raw lines 28-49; source lines 19, 23-28).

Unchanged termination and merchant duties include breach of prohibited categories or unremedied high disputes, Klarna as payee on customer documents without merchant bank details, no Klarna surcharges/unfairness, obeying stop/shipping instructions, trademark boundaries and exclusion of financially interested purchasers (old raw lines 26-39; new raw lines 36-49; source lines 21-28).

Both captures say Australian businesses actively promoting/recommending Pay in 4 might be considered DDO distributors and might have duties; the current source and BNPL concept incorrectly state they are distributors and must comply without the modal qualification. This is a pre-existing summary error, separate from the raw delta, and the TMD/significant-adverse-dealing/reporting duties remain conditional or on request (old raw lines 41-50; new raw lines 51-60; source line 30; wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md line 213).
substantive_changes: Expanded Klarna-specific prohibited categories beyond the three in the 2026-05-06 capture, with the B2B/BTB label discrepancy preserved (old raw lines 10-18; new raw lines 11-26).

New EU consumer credit marketing CCD2 disclosure statement with prospective 2026-11-20 applicability and country-specific Klarna-guideline links, not present in old capture (old raw lines 20-24; new raw lines 28-34).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the old 2026-05-06 three-category list and UK approved-messaging/AU DDO guidance as dated, not as a complete current prohibition list (old raw lines 10-24, 41-50; new raw lines 11-34, 51-60).

Retain the continuing Klarna customer-eligibility/payment-rights distinction, Stripe merchant-acquiring/settlement role, termination and merchant duties; display of PMME is not payment approval or comprehensive legal compliance proof (old raw lines 20-39; new raw lines 28-49).
conflicts: Current source and BNPL concept list only charities/political organizations/B2B for Klarna-specific prohibitions (source line 17; wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md line 207), while the new capture adds seven category groups (new raw lines 13-24). Add reciprocal dated warnings, not an inferred broad exclusion for every possible business subcategory.

Current source says Australian active promoters are distributors and must follow/report (source line 30), as does wiki/concepts/stripe-bnpl.md line 213; both old and new raw use 'might' for distributor status and consequent duties (old raw lines 41-50; new raw lines 51-60). Correct this baseline overstatement separately.

Current source says PMME 'handles compliance automatically' after the UK FCA sentence (source line 19), while raw only says it automatically handles Klarna brand compliance and still separately requires approved UK messaging and, in new capture, applicable EU disclosures (old raw lines 20-24; new raw lines 28-34). Scope that automation claim to branding rather than all regulatory obligations.
unresolved_questions: This review-only local capture does not independently verify current law, each country guideline's contents, or a specific merchant's classification/eligibility; the prospective 2026-11-20 CCD2 claim must remain attributed to the 2026-11-07 Stripe page (new raw lines 26-34).

The B2B versus BTB spelling difference is not explained by the capture; treat it as a wording discrepancy pending provider clarification rather than a policy change (old raw line 16; new raw line 17).

findings: Add exact canonical URL and 2026-11-07 raw provenance while retaining the 2026-05-06 capture; expand the prohibition list and add a date/scope-qualified EU CCD2 marketing disclosure locator (source lines 1-34; old raw lines 10-24; new raw lines 11-34).

Retain UK marketing, termination and merchant-duty facts, but restore Australia's conditional 'might' and scope PMME to brand compliance (source lines 19-30; old raw lines 20-50; new raw lines 28-60).
conflicts: Existing three-item prohibition list is incomplete relative to new capture (source line 17; new raw lines 13-24).
Source's definite Australian distributor/duty language overstates both captures' conditional language (source line 30; old raw lines 41-50; new raw lines 51-60).
source_assessments.reason: The new page materially changes prohibited-category and EU marketing guidance, while the old source contains a separate modal baseline error requiring correction.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna/compliance, the new capture describes Klarna network eligibility and merchant marketing obligations, not a payment API or account approval. Beyond Stripe-wide restrictions it prohibits charities, political groups, B2B (spelled BTB in the new page), money/crypto services, stored value, insolvency/debt/fines/bail, gambling, direct marketing and fundraising categories (new raw lines 11-26; old raw lines 10-18). UK promotion requires Klarna-approved messaging; a new EU-consumer credit marketing paragraph says CCD2 disclosures apply beginning 2026-11-20 with pre-approved copy and country guidance (new raw lines 28-34). Klarna decides customer use and receives customer payment rights; Stripe acquires and settles merchant funds, distinct from displaying a message or requesting eligibility (new raw lines 36-49). Australian DDO distributor status and duties are conditional (new raw lines 51-60). source-stripe-klarna-compliance.md omits new categories/EU scope and overstates that conditional Australian status (source lines 17-30).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna/compliance, expanded prohibited categories and the dated EU CCD2 consumer-credit marketing disclosure statement are substantive (old raw lines 10-24; new raw lines 11-34). The UK guideline destination change, heading space and B2B-to-BTB label wording alone are navigation/wording, not evidence of a new B2B policy. Keep source-stripe-klarna-compliance.md's 2026-05-06 UK, termination and merchant duties dated, add the new 2026-11-07 category and prospective 2026-11-20 claims, and correct its pre-existing 'are distributors' overstatement because both captures say 'might' (old raw lines 41-50; new raw lines 51-60). PMME brand handling does not prove all UK/EU legal compliance; Dashboard settings do not prove merchant eligibility, and marketing display or provider customer-eligibility decisions do not prove payment success or settlement.
